gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-ysabeau-infant: Red Hat Display draws every line like a marker, one width throughout, with daylight showing inside each curve. Ysabeau Infant follows, its outward-pointing terminals like tongs.
gen-almendra-display-fs-asap: Almendra Display is ornate and literary, with a tall x-height and letters that never pinch shut. Asap follows in sans-serif, its open arcs and near-capital lowercase keeping things easy to follow.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-fs-technor: Tilt Neon sets down a tube-like, constant-width stroke with a splayed c terminal and a big x-height. And Technor, glowing in plain sans lines, would swallow that presence if the heading were made small.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-yaldevi: Yaldevi has a clean sans voice, with an e opening clearly to the right. Wallpoet earns its keep big and short, where its high-rising lowercase and the paper showing between letters can stand out.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-ubuntu-sans: Stretched out and fearless. Warnes tapers its ink strokes before they touch, while Ubuntu Sans answers with tubular, copper-pipe lines and washer-sized lowercase eyes that keep the page grounded.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-sulphur-point: Sulphur Point keeps a marker-like line and bulky lowercase. Luckiest Guy brings the loud, poured-ink cheer above it, and together the two are chunky and friendly, with open gaps that never clog.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-alegreya-sans-sc: Chubbo looks drawn with a marker tip, casual and inviting. Alegreya Sans SC follows in a modern sans with an open gap in the c, so a longer passage would move along easily.
gen-press-start-2p-fs-technor: Technor reads cool and geometric, with neon-tube lines and a wide channel into every bowl, a quiet glow on the page. Press Start 2P brings the retro fun; Technor brings the steadiness.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-savate: Savate reads clean and contemporary, with a tall rounded o and open jaws on its curves. Unica One adds a commanding, large-eyed lowercase above it, and the sturdy hairlines hold their own beside it.
gen-irish-grover-gf-sen: Sen traces tall lowercase with a line of constant weight, curves ending before they turn inward. And Irish Grover is the fun, organic one, its sturdy tall words softened by slightly lighter joins.
